## Summary

Run deterministic instruction-surface Evals (F050 Evidence; F058).

## Usage

```bash
amber eval <run|list|show|admit> --target <repo> [--json]
       amber eval run --target <repo> [--suite instruction-surface] [--json]
       amber eval admit --target <repo> --producer <principal> [--suite instruction-surface] [--definition-id <identity>] [--outcome-id <identity>] [--evidence-id <id>] [--subject <subject>] --yes [--json]
       amber eval list --target <repo> [--json]
       amber eval show --id <evalId> --target <repo> [--json]
```

## Command Details

```text
Run deterministic instruction-surface Evals (F050 Evidence; F058).
Version 2 contains four Evals: MCP tool descriptions, QA contract-surface
model independence, the Context quote boundary, and breadcrumb authenticity.
`eval run` is report-only; `eval admit` is the explicit F050 admission path
that writes canonical Eval definition/result artifacts and a replayable
Evidence receipt. Eval is not Approval and cannot widen execution authority.

Subcommands:
  run [--suite instruction-surface]  Replay the suite against --target.
        Exit 0 when every Eval passes; exit 1 when any Eval has findings.
  admit --producer <principal>  Admit the suite definition/result artifacts
        and record replayable Evidence through the normal receipt ledger.
        Optional: --definition-id, --outcome-id, --evidence-id, --subject.
  list                  List registered Eval identities in the suite.
  show --id <evalId>    Show one Eval definition.

Examples:
  amber eval run --target . --json
  amber eval admit --target . --producer ci-runner --evidence-id evidence/eval-run --yes --json
  amber eval list --target .
  amber eval show --id eval.instruction-surface.mcp-tool-description --target .
```

## Boundaries & Safety

- `--target <path>` selects repository state. Amber confines these target-relative paths, refusing `..` and symlink escapes before reading or writing: plan and scaffold destinations (including `accept --plan`), memory and context payloads, harness inputs, adapter allow-lists, workflow reports and their output directory, ledger exports, execution readiness plans, session and worktree state, governance report output, wiki export and handoff bundle output directories.
- Path validation is not OS sandboxing, and the confinement above covers only the surfaces it names, and a confined flag still accepts an absolute destination only when it stays inside the target. `governance audit --output`, `governance readiness --output`, `security audit --output`, `loop record --output`, and `explain --markdown` resolve against the working directory instead of `--target`. A path flag not listed here is confined only when the command that reads it routes through the boundary. A governed or verification command still runs with your user's file permissions.
- `wiki export`, `handoff bundle`, and `workflow assess` reject output directories that resolve to the target root, including `.`, an absolute root path, `nested/..`, and symlink or junction aliases of the root. Output subdirectories and defaults are unchanged.
- `handoff validate --bundle-dir .` and `workflow assess --handoff-bundle-dir .` still accept root-level bundles as read-only inputs.
- **Fail-Closed Behavior**: Corrupt governance state or invalid schema parameters immediately halt execution with non-zero exit codes.
